entry.name: Priest in the Samaritan parable
entry.note: Unnamed priest inside the narrated story in Luke 10:31, who sees the traveler and passes on the other side. Distinct from every named priest elsewhere and from the framing speakers.

result.appearanceFromText: The text fixes only that he is a priest traveling down the road from Jerusalem to Jericho who passes by on the other side; no physical features are given, so the priestly dress follows the brief's Roman Judea clothing (priestly robes) and the age, build and features are invented in a plain, era-appropriate way.

stages.label: Priest in the Samaritan parable
stages.when: Roman Judea, the road from Jerusalem to Jericho

quotes.quote: By chance a certain priest was going down that way.

stages.text: Priest in the Samaritan parable: a man of middle years with a lean, weathered build and dark, short-cropped hair and a close-trimmed beard streaked with grey. Sun-browned skin and a serious, careful face. He wears a long priestly robe of undyed linen with a dark woven sash and a fringed prayer shawl over the shoulders, in muted ochre and off-white. He carries nothing in his hands but a small leather scrip at his side.
